gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Chaotic and raw, Disorder spreads its tall lowercase glyphs far apart, with no swelling where curves meet stems. Noto Sans Arabic handles the quieter work, with wide openings on small letters and a clean, modern plainness.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-armenia: Noto Sans Armenian is approachable and wide-mouthed on its round letters, its lowercase standing tall and full. Disorder is best at raw, chaotic display with its glyphs flung apart, while the plain sans is best at staying inviting.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Disorder never swells or tapers a stroke, and its big lowercase sits well apart. Noto Sans Avestan is the foil, modern and clean, with curve tips that stop short of touching.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-balines: Noto Sans Balinese reads modern and professional, with breathing space inside every curve. Next to it, Disorder feels raw and chaotic, glyphs set well apart, curves meeting stems without swelling.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Disorder draws neon-tube strokes that never change width. Noto Sans Bamum is the modern, clean partner, its curves ending before they turn inward and its small letters full of open counters.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-bassa-v: Noto Sans Bassa Vah reads contemporary, with a dominant midsection that swallows the line's height. But Disorder is the one with the standout trait, a stroke with no contrast at all, raw against that sans.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-batak: Chaotic, raw, and flat of stroke, that's Disorder. Noto Sans Batak, towering in the lowercase and generous in its e, carries paragraph after paragraph with an approachable, unsqueezed feel.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Loud, loose and unshaded, Disorder rings its o's with one constant wall and spaces everything out. But Noto Sans Bengali is the sans-serif that does the quiet work, capitals barely taller than lowercase and letter mouths distinctly open.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksu: Disorder outlines every letter with one steady thickness, spacing its big lowercase glyphs well apart and leaving curves unswollen. Disorder shouts; Noto Sans Bhaiksuki, with open apertures, simply reads.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Contemporary in feel, Noto Sans Brahmi keeps its mean line set high and leaves every curved letter open-ended. And Disorder, drawn as if with a fixed pen and spaced well apart, gives that sans a raw, chaotic partner.
